title: Collapsible rail task-centric IA and deprecation plan
content:
Purpose: capture a pragmatic redesign for the left rail that centers tasks (what users want to do) rather than products or models, and also include an explicit, low-risk route deprecation plan for legacy paths. This is a working grooming doc — notes, wireframe callouts, and backlog items.

Background and why now:
- Console growth has made the left rail noisy: every feature team adds a link, users report hunting for actions instead of finding them.
- Recent customer interviews (PLG power users, infra SREs, solutions engineers) show the most common mental model is "task-first" (deploy, observe, debug, cost-optimize).
- We need a migration approach that: preserves deep links, supports canary paging, and yields measurable navigation success metrics.

Guiding principles:
1) Tasks over product namespaces: surface "Create deployment", "Inspect traces", "Run evals", "Manage capacity" as primary anchors.
2) Progressive disclosure: collapsed rail with icon-only mode, hover peek, and a persistent quick-actions popover (cmd/ctrl+K) for power users.
3) Predictable routing: canonical routes per task and a single stable path for exchange across SDKs and docs. Legacy routes redirect with a 302-style client redirect and analytics capture.
4) Backwards compatibility window: 6 weeks soft deprecation (warning banner), 8 weeks hard redirect + telemetry check.

Proposed rail composition (left to right):
- Global actions (top): Search, Quick New (+), Global Settings
- Workspaces & org switcher (collapsible section)
- Task anchors (sticky): Deployments, Runs & Jobs, Observability, Models, Cost & Quotas, Access & Security
- Utilities (bottom): Notifications, Help & Docs, Feedback

Wireframe callouts (desktop):
- Collapsed width: 64px; Expanded: 280px.
- Hover peek: partial expansion showing label for hovered item with micro-delay 200ms.
- Selected anchor shows contextual mini-panel on right (300–420px) with top-level actions (create, filters, recent).
- Keyboard: left-rail focus ring, j/k for next/prev anchor, enter to open anchor, shift+enter to open in new tab.

Routing and deprecation plan (draft):
- Map of old -> new canonical routes (example):
  /enterprise/models -> /models (canonical)
  /apps/deploy -> /deployments/new (canonical)
- Soft deprecation: when user hits old route show unobtrusive banner: "This link is being consolidated" with a "Go to new" CTA and a "Keep using old path" option. Record event CONS.route_deprecation.click.
- Hard redirect: after 8 weeks client-side redirect to canonical route. Provide server-side 301s for external crawlers and docs links.
- Telemetry checks: retention of successful redirects, top 10 legacy routes, error spikes. Rollback plan: revert redirect and extend soft phase.

Backlog grooming (initial tickets and priority):
- CONS-1452: canonical route mapping + redirect table (P0)
- CONS-1457: collapsed rail component + hover peek microcopy (P1)
- CONS-1461: persistent quick-actions popover + keyboard shortcuts (P1)
- CONS-1465: tenant-level workspace switcher + animation perf (P2)
- CONS-1470: analytics events and dashboard (nav success, time-to-action) (P0)

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Do we include model-specific quick actions in task anchors (e.g., "Run eval on model X") or keep model actions in the Models page? (security: shortcut may surface restricted models).
- Mobile behaviour: collapse to bottom nav or keep hamburger -> deferred to mobile UX spike.
- How aggressive should auto-redirects be for saved bookmarks? default: conservative (soft then hard).

Rollout proposal (phased):
1) Internal dogfood (team + SRE): feature-flagged collapsed rail + analytics (2 weeks)
2) Beta (selected PLG orgs + partners): enable task anchors and soft deprecation banners (4 weeks)
3) Gradual rollout + A/B: track nav success and task completion; run canary on 5% increments (6 weeks)
4) Full rollout + hard redirects after telemetry gates

Acceptance metrics (what success looks like):
- 15% reduction in mean time-to-first-action for new users in the console within 4 weeks.
- 10% fewer support tickets for "where is X" flow.
- Low regression in task completion for heavy users (<=3% drop).

Next immediate steps (this week):
- Groom CONS-1452 and assign canonical route owners (Priya + Marco).
- Quick prototype of collapsed rail interactions in Figma (Sofia).
- Instrument initial analytics events (Ben) and add a dashboard in observability.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add sample redirect header snippets for docs team (Nginx + CloudFront examples).
- Draft customer-facing migration note and support KB.
- Schedule sync with Solutions Eng to identify high-value bookmarks to preserve.

References and context links included in metadata. This doc is intentionally terse — intended as a grooming artifact for the Console IA sprint.
